clue.text: Endlessly talk about what may be thrown

indicators.note: endlessly means the synonym for talk about loses its final letter

parts.note: to talk about a topic is to discuss it

explanation.surface: Someone speculates about which object might get hurled during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last S from DISCUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is the heavy disc that athletes hurl in a field event.

clue.text: Model inside a little bottle

indicators.note: to bottle is to keep something enclosed, so these words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A ship model is stuck inside a small bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' seems to be the container signal, but 'bottle' is: 'inside a little' bottles the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a perfect example or standard to copy.

clue.text: Vessel of tin containing a flower

indicators.note: containing means the tin holds the other letters

parts.note: a can is a tin
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Tamar divides Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A tin pot holds a single bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick: a thing that flows, here the River Tamar in south-west England. 'Containing' puts A TAMAR inside CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, a kind of craft.

clue.text: Air the cabin

explanation.surface: Someone opens the windows to freshen a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like a verb, ventilate; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailors' work song, a tune; it is also a crude shack or hut.

clue.text: Overlord, for instance, once made wild

indicators.note: wild means the letters of the words once made run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A tyrant who once ran things has been driven mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Overlord was the Allies' secret label for the 1944 Normandy invasion; 'wild' rearranges ONCE MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Operation Overlord was the wartime cover label used for the D-Day landings, an example of a secret title.

clue.text: Rich person threw out this designer

indicators.note: threw out signals the letters are thrown about into another order

explanation.surface: A wealthy client ejects the architect from the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges RICH PERSON THREW into the architect of St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The man named was the architect who planned St Paul's Cathedral and many London churches.

clue.text: County players are dejected

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: A local team's members are feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County players' looks like a cricket team; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, dispirited.

clue.text: August coming up — the time for weight to intrude

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from the bottom
to intrude means the weight abbreviation pushes into the word for an age

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time
lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: Late summer approaches, the season for scales to creep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To intrude' puts LB into EON, making ELBON; 'coming up' turns that around. 'August' wants to be the month; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means dignified and majestic, like an aristocrat.

clue.text: Plant remains in front of school

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: what remains is the rest
Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone stays put at a factory near a school gate.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a famous fee-paying boys' school in north-west London. 'Plant' wants to be a factory; it is a botanical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Restharrow is a pink-flowered wild shrub of the pea family, a kind of vegetation.

clue.text: Eager (according to some) to drill a well

explanation.surface: A keen person sets out to sink a well.
explanation.walkthrough: An eagre (also spelt eager) is a tidal wave surging up an estuary, as on the Severn; '(according to some)' marks that spelling as a variant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge up a river is called a bore or eagre; to sink a shaft by drilling is to bore.

clue.text: Around mountain top somewhere to fasten rope is needed by climber

indicators.note: around means the rope fastening wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a cleat is a fitting that a rope is tied off on

indicators.note: top means the highest, first letter of mountain

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs a fixing point on a summit for the rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' wants to be the mountaineer; it is a climbing plant. 'Around' puts M inside CLEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a woody vine that scrambles up walls and trellises, a classic climbing plant.

clue.text: Connecticut will accept a Russian, I trust

indicators.note: will accept means the state abbreviation takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Connecticut
a Red is a Soviet-era Russian communist
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American state is hoping to welcome a Russian visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will accept' puts RED and I inside CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit as a verb means believe or have faith in someone's word.

clue.text: State welcome given to monarch

indicators.note: given to puts the greeting before the monarch's letter

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A ruler receives a greeting from the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' wants to be a country; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly.

clue.text: Changeable — not quite inclined to come into line

indicators.note: to come into means the trimmed word goes inside the word for a line of poetry

parts.note: a verse is a line of poetry

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: atilt means tipped, inclined

explanation.surface: Someone fickle, half-willing to fall into step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims ATILT to ATIL; 'to come into' puts that inside VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile means adaptable and able to turn readily from one thing to another.

clue.text: One watching outside broadcast — one opening the rally

parts.note: in tennis the server starts each rally

explanation.surface: A TV crew filming on location sees the first shot of a tennis point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' suggests a political meeting; it is an exchange of shots in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is a spectator or onlooker who takes note of events.

clue.text: Best o' fare when properly cooked

definitions.text: Best o' fare when properly cooked

indicators.note: properly cooked means the letters of the words best o' fare are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: The finest food, done just right, is the traditional English joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properly cooked' rearranges BEST O' FARE; the whole clue also describes the dish, a traditional English Sunday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday joint from an ox is often called the best English fare when well done.

clue.text: Cashiers with it meant to make light of the main opposition

definitions.text: meant to make light of the main opposition

parts.note: to cashier someone is to dismiss or fire them
it means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Bank tellers who are trendy try to laugh off their chief rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' means set alight, not belittle, and 'the main' is the sea: such a vessel was set burning and sent among enemy ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireship was a burning vessel set adrift toward an enemy fleet to set it ablaze.

clue.text: A course of husky food makes us flourish

parts.note: bran is the husks of cereal grain, food made of husks
a dish is one course of a meal

explanation.surface: A hearty dish of sled-dog chow cheers everyone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' suggests a sled dog; it means made of husks, as bran is. The held clue carried a stray '8A' at the start, which the page does not print.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword or stick is to wave it about showily.

clue.text: Does book…

explanation.surface: Someone performs a reading from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue on into 21 across, but this answer stands alone. Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to do or perform; the Acts is a New Testament book that follows the Gospels.

clue.text: Glances a second — nothing to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard means the spoken form of the next pieces gives the answer

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second; nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a quick look for a moment but hears nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a snick is a faint edge off the bat, a glancing contact. 'Glances' wants to be quick looks.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, to snick is to edge the ball off the bat at a slight deflection.

clue.text: …found by the French keep part of this?

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Continuing from 19, the French discover a book where a stronghold is the setting.
explanation.walkthrough: A keep is the central tower of a fortress, so the keep is part of this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest tower within a fortified medieval stronghold.

clue.text: Formidable opponent, grand in a row

indicators.note: in puts the letter for grand inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A tough rival has a big quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger, figuratively, is a fierce, aggressive competitor.

clue.text: 22 run riot, and appear genuine

indicators.note: run riot signals that these letters go out of control into a fresh order

parts.note: the answer to 22 down, a big striped cat

explanation.surface: A big cat on the loose seems convincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 down is TIGER; 'riot' scrambles TIGER plus RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring true is an idiom for sounding sincere or credible.

clue.text: Thrown out of bed earlier than arranged

indicators.note: earlier than puts the first piece before the second

parts.note: to be up is to be out of bed
set means arranged or fixed

explanation.surface: Someone tossed out of bed before the alarm went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' here means disconcerted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thrown is to be disconcerted, unsettled.

clue.text: Royal family go without nothing

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: without means take away the letter for zero

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A royal household carries on with nothing to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' takes O out of GO, leaving G.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male monarch, the highest member of a ruling house.

clue.text: It may find its way into a trap-what bad luck!

definitions.text: It may find its way into a trap

explanation.surface: A piece of bait ends up in a mousetrap, and someone says what a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: A firm cheese is the classic mousetrap bait; the phrase is also a British, often ironic, way to say tough luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm cheddar is cartoon bait for mice; hard cheese is also British slang meaning too bad, tough luck.

clue.text: Aquatic creature beginning to proliferate in the ground

indicators.note: in means the first letter of proliferate goes inside the word for land

parts.note: terrain is ground, a stretch of land

indicators.note: beginning to means the opening letter of proliferate

explanation.surface: A water animal starts breeding wildly in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts P inside TERRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle.

clue.text: American football player's old bicycle

explanation.surface: A gridiron player rides an antique bike.
explanation.walkthrough: In American football a safety is a defensive back; the safety bicycle of the 1880s replaced the penny-farthing.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety names a defensive back position on a gridiron team and the early chain-driven bicycle with equal wheels.
